summary: Prioritize cosmic and macro-physics topics like planetary orbits which significantly outperform molecular chemistry or biology in initial view attraction.
Formulate hooks that jump straight into a direct paradox or counter-intuitive question within the first 5 words, avoiding preamble phrases like 'You've used...'.
Keep video durations strictly under 35 seconds to prevent steep audience drop-off and maintain higher average view percentages.
Draft titles that state a direct, high-stakes curiosity gap without appending lengthy explanatory subtitles.
Eliminate conversational filler at the beginning of the first sentence, ensuring immediate cognitive engagement for the Shorts feed test window.
winning_hooks: If the Sun pulls the Earth, why don't we just crash into it?
A 10kg lead sphere and a 1kg lead sphere dropped from the same height in a vacuum. Why don't they hit the ground at different moments?
avoid: Opening hooks with familiar observations like 'You've seen...' or 'You've used...' which yield low stayed percentages.
Exceeding 40 seconds in duration for explanatory science topics.
Complex multi-clause opening sentences that delay the core question past the 3-second retention window.
next_experiment: Test an astrophysics topic under 30 seconds using an extreme direct-question hook ('Why doesn't the moon crash into Earth?') versus a longer narrative hook to isolate length and topic impact on stayed_pct.
